newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '97 manufacturing output seen up 12.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '97 manufacturing output seen up 12.5 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's manufacturing sector production is forecast to rise by 12.5 percent in 1997, against an estimated 12.8 percent increase in 1996, the Ministry of Finance said on Friday in its 1996/97 economic report.
In 1995, the sector's output grew by 14.5 percent.

"The moderation in manufacturing output was due to some deceleration in the growth of export-oriented industries, particularly electronics in tandem with the global trend," the ministry said in its annual report.
Output of the electrical, electronics and machinery industry rose at a much slower rate of 10.4 percent during the first seven months of 1996 versus a 23.8 percent gain in the comparable 1995 period.
Electronics and electrical goods are Malaysia's single biggest export item, accounting for around 15 percent of total exports.

Semiconductor and other electronic components registered a weaker output growth of 17.2 percent from January to July 1996, versus 27.4 percent growth in the first seven months of 1995, due to softening demand growth for products such as Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) chips, the report said.
A high level of global inventories since late 1995 has contributed to the slump in the electronics industry.

Production in the construction sector is estimated to rise by 8.8 percent in 1997, versus an estimated 9.0 percent gain in 1996. In 1995, the industry's output jumped by 17.3 percent, the report said.

Slower growth in the sector was due to a moderation in public and private sector investment as well as measures introduced last year to discourage asset speculation and the purchase of real estate by foreigners, the report said.
On the services side, output was projected to grow by 8.7 percent in 1997, after an estimated 8.9 percent expansion in 1996. In 1995, the sector's production grew by 9.4 percent.
